# Airscale API full documentation

> Airscale product guides, integration workflows, MCP documentation, and public API reference.
> This is the full public, navigable preview corpus. It remains intentionally noindex for traditional search engines.

## API Overview

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/api-overview.md

Description: Authenticate with Airscale and make your first API request.

Use the Airscale API to search for people and companies and enrich contact data from your application.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Make your first request" href="/api-reference/credit-count">
    Check your workspace's remaining credits with a request that has no body.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Browse endpoints" href="/api-reference/find-people">
    Start with people search, then explore company search and enrichment endpoints.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Make your first request

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create an API key">
    In Airscale, open **Settings → API key** and create a key for your server-side application.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Authenticate">
    Store the key in an environment variable and send it as a Bearer token on every request.

    ```bash
    export AIRSCALE_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Request your credit balance">
    Call `POST https://api.airscale.io/v1/credits` with no body.

    ```bash cURL
    curl --request POST \
      --url https://api.airscale.io/v1/credits \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer $AIRSCALE_API_KEY"
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

A successful request returns the remaining workspace balance as a number:

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "response": {
    "credits": 1200
  }
}
```

## Authentication

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/authentication.md

Description: Create, send, protect, and rotate an Airscale API key.

Airscale authenticates API requests with a workspace API key sent as a Bearer token.

## Create an API key

Create the key in **Airscale Settings**: open the [Airscale dashboard](https://app.airscale.io/dashboard), choose **Settings → API key**, and generate a key for your integration.

Store the value in your server's secret manager or environment configuration:

```bash
export AIRSCALE_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
```

## Send the key

Include this header on every API request:

```text
Authorization: Bearer $AIRSCALE_API_KEY
```

## Handle unauthorized requests

A missing Bearer token or an invalid API key returns `401 Unauthorized`. Check that the header is present, that it starts with `Bearer`, and that your deployed secret contains the current key before retrying.

<Warning>
Keep API keys server-side. Never commit them to source control, place them in examples, or expose them in browser or mobile client bundles.
</Warning>

## Rotate a compromised key

If a key is exposed, rotate it immediately in **Airscale Settings**. Update the server-side secret, deploy the new value, verify an authenticated request, and stop using the old key.

Next, review [Rate limits](/api-reference/rate-limits) before adding request concurrency or retries.

---

## Rate limits

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/rate-limits.md

Description: Understand endpoint-specific request limits and 429 responses.

Airscale rate limits are endpoint-specific. Each endpoint can enforce a different request limit and time window, so use the value documented on the endpoint page you are calling.

## Handle rate-limit responses

When a request exceeds an endpoint's limit, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Treat the status code as the rate-limit signal; do not depend on an error field or response header unless that endpoint page documents it.

Only retry when the endpoint page says the operation is safe to retry. Use bounded exponential backoff: cap both the maximum delay and the total number of attempts, then surface a persistent `429` to your application.

## Check an endpoint's limit

Review the request limit on the endpoint page before setting concurrency:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Find people" href="/api-reference/find-people">
    People search limits and request contract.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Find companies" href="/api-reference/find-companies">
    Company search limits and request contract.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Email finder" href="/api-reference/email-finder">
    Professional email lookup limits and request contract.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Airsearch" href="/api-reference/airsearch">
    Airsearch limits and request contract.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Find people

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/find-people.md

Description: Search people using person, role, and company filters.

Search for people using person, role, current-company, and past-experience filters, then page through the matching lead records.

<Note>
The Search and [Count people](/api-reference/find-people/count) operations share a limit of 6 requests per second per workspace. Search costs 0.1 credits per returned lead; empty result pages are not charged. Count accepts the same `query` for free.
</Note>

Search returns at most 100 leads per request. When `next_cursor` is not `null`, send it unchanged as `cursor` with the same `query`. Do not derive or edit cursor contents.

After a `429`, wait for the next second and retry with bounded exponential backoff. A failed search or credit-service attempt does not return charged leads.

## Next step

Use [Count people](/api-reference/find-people/count) to estimate the audience for free, [Find companies](/api-reference/find-companies) to discover organizations, or [Rate limits](/api-reference/rate-limits) before adding concurrency.

---

## Count people

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/find-people/count.md

Description: Count people matching person, role, and company filters.

Estimate an audience before retrieving any lead records. Count accepts the same person, role, current-company, and past-experience filters as [Find people](/api-reference/find-people).

<Note>
Count is free. It neither reserves nor debits Airscale credits, and its response contains only the matching total.
</Note>

## Reuse a search audience

Send the same `query` object you plan to use for Find people. Count has no pagination fields because it returns no lead page; keep `size` and `cursor` on the search request instead.

The Count and Find people operations share a limit of 6 requests per second per workspace. After a `429 Too Many Requests` response, wait for the next second and retry with bounded exponential backoff.

<Info>
This preview renders non-executing examples. It does not send a request or ask for an API key.
</Info>

## Next step

Use [Find people](/api-reference/find-people) with the same `query` when you are ready to retrieve the matching records.

---

## Find companies

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/find-companies.md

Description: Search companies using firmographic, location, event, intent, and technology filters.

Search companies by firmographic, location, event, intent, and technology filters, then page through the matching organizations.

<Note>
Search shares a limit of 6 requests per second per workspace with [Company filter values](/api-reference/find-companies/filter-values). It costs 0.1 credits per returned company; zero returned rows cost zero credits. At least 0.1 credits must be available before Search begins.
</Note>

When `next_cursor` is not `null`, send the exact value unchanged as `cursor` with the same filters. Do not decode, construct, or edit the cursor. Cursor pagination preserves the original page size and can traverse up to 10,000 companies for one search.

After a `429`, wait for the next second and retry with bounded exponential backoff. Retry a settlement failure only after the credit service recovers.

## Next step

Use [Company filter values](/api-reference/find-companies/filter-values) to discover accepted values, [Find people](/api-reference/find-people) to search for roles at identified companies, or [Authentication](/api-reference/authentication) before integrating.

---

## Company filter values

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/find-companies/filter-values.md

Description: Search supported values for Find Companies filters.

Discover accepted values before adding a city, region, industry, topic, or technology filter to [Find companies](/api-reference/find-companies).

<Note>
Filter-values is free and has no request body. It does not reserve or debit Airscale credits.
</Note>

## Choose useful context

Use `country` and `region` to narrow location suggestions. A bare region name needs country context. The `q` parameter takes precedence when both `q` and its `query` alias are present; a blank `q` still suppresses `query` and returns `400 Bad Request`.

The operation shares a limit of 6 requests per second per workspace with Find companies. After a `429 Too Many Requests` response, wait for the next second and retry with bounded exponential backoff.

<Info>
This preview renders non-executing examples. It does not send a request or ask for an API key.
</Info>

## Next step

Copy the returned `value` into the matching filter on [Find companies](/api-reference/find-companies).

---

## Airsearch

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/airsearch.md

Description: Research the web and return structured answers with Airsearch.

Ask a research question and receive a sourced answer, with optional output fields shaped for your application.

<Note>
The limit is 300 requests per minute per workspace. A `success` result costs 1 credit; `not_found` and `timeout` are not charged. The reservation is settled only for `success` and released for the other completed statuses.
</Note>

Requested schema keys are optional and nullable. Structured numeric and boolean values are returned as strings when present, so parse them explicitly when your application requires native scalar types.

A later-stage soft timeout returns `200 OK` with `status: "timeout"`. An initial-stage timeout returns `504 Gateway Timeout`; narrow the prompt before retrying. Use bounded backoff for transient dependency failures.

## Next step

Use [Find companies](/api-reference/find-companies) when the research target should come from structured firmographic filters, or review [Rate limits](/api-reference/rate-limits) before adding parallel requests.

---

## Email finder

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/email-finder.md

Description: Find a professional email address for one person.

Identify one person by LinkedIn profile URL or by name and company, then return a verified professional email when one is found.

<Note>
The limit is 3,000 requests per minute per workspace. A successful result costs 2 credits; `not_found` is not charged.
</Note>

At least one complete identification form is required. You may send both forms when you have them.

<Warning>
Use bounded backoff after a transient `502` or `503`. A `503` can mean a successful result could not be settled by the credit service; retry the same input only after the service recovers.
</Warning>

## Next step

Use [Bulk email finder](/api-reference/email-finder-(bulk)) when you need asynchronous results for up to 100 people.

---

## Bulk email finder

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/email-finder-(bulk).md

Description: Find professional email addresses for a batch of people.

Submit up to 100 people and receive one asynchronous professional-email result per item at your webhook.

<Note>
The limit is 3,000 input items per minute per workspace. Each item with `status: "success"` costs 2 credits; misses and timeouts are not charged.
</Note>

The acceptance response only confirms that the batch was queued. Processing continues after that response, and each item is delivered separately to `webhook_url`.

## Webhook callbacks

Every callback echoes `custom_id`. When the submitted value is omitted or `null`, Airscale uses that item's zero-based input index.

- A found email has `status: "success"`, the resolved `email`, `email_status: "valid"`, and the public `provider` and `verifier` labels.
- An item skipped after the remaining batch balance drops below 2 credits has `status: "error"`, `error: "insufficient_credits"`, and `email: null`.
- A miss or exhausted lookup has `status: "not_found"` or `status: "timeout"`, respectively, with `email: null`.

<Warning>
Return a `2xx` response promptly for every callback. Automatic webhook retries are not part of this operation's contract, so persist callbacks and use `custom_id` to reconcile expected and received results.
</Warning>

Add credits before submitting skipped items again.

## Next step

Use [Email finder](/api-reference/email-finder) for a synchronous single-person lookup, or review [Rate limits](/api-reference/rate-limits) before batching requests.

---

## Mobile finder

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/mobile-finder.md

Description: Find a mobile phone number from a professional profile.

Submit a LinkedIn person profile URL and return a mobile phone number when one is found.

<Note>
The limit is 3,000 requests per minute per workspace. A successful result costs 40 credits; `not_found` is not charged.
</Note>

Use bounded backoff for transient failures. If a successful result could not be settled by the credit service, retry the same input only after the service recovers.

## Next step

Use [Personal email](/api-reference/personal-email) to look for a personal address from the same profile, or [Reverse phone](/api-reference/reverse-phone) when the phone number is your starting point.

---

## Personal email

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/personal-email.md

Description: Find a personal email address from a professional profile.

Submit a LinkedIn person profile URL and return a personal email address when one is found.

<Note>
The limit is 2,000 requests per minute per workspace. The minimum balance required to start is 3 credits. A successful result costs between 3 and 12 credits, depending on its source; `not_found` costs 0 credits.
</Note>

<Warning>
If a result is found and charged but required usage recording then fails, the operation returns `502 Bad Gateway`. Check your balance before retrying that input to avoid paying again for the same result.
</Warning>

For other transient failures, retry with bounded backoff. Wait for the credit service to recover before retrying a settlement failure.

## Next step

Use [People URL finder](/api-reference/people-url-finder) when you have a name and company but no profile URL.

---

## People URL finder

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/people-url-finder.md

Description: Find a professional profile URL from person and company details.

Identify a person by first name, last name, and company, then return a matching professional profile URL when one is found.

<Note>
The limit is 6 requests per second per workspace. A successful result costs 0.5 credits; `not_found` is not charged.
</Note>

After a `429 Too Many Requests` response, retry in a later second with bounded exponential backoff. Retry transient reservation failures with the same input only after the service recovers.

## Next step

Pass the matched URL to [Email finder](/api-reference/email-finder) for professional email enrichment.

---

## People profile

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/extract-people-profile.md

Description: Extract a structured person profile from a professional profile URL.

Extract a structured person profile from a recognized LinkedIn URL, normally an `/in/` profile.

<Note>
The limit is 3,000 requests per minute per workspace. The submitted URL selects the response schema and successful-call credit cost: `/in/` successes cost 1 credit by default, while `/company/` and `/school/` successes cost 0.5 credits. Workspace-specific pricing can differ, and unsuccessful requests are not charged.
</Note>

The optional modes are `p1`, `p2`, and `p3`. Omit `mode` for the default extraction workflow, whose successful shape can vary; use `p2` or `p3` when you need the normalized schema. The submitted URL, not the route name, selects person versus company output.

Extraction failures return an error rather than a `200 OK` no-result envelope. Retry transient extraction or settlement failures with bounded backoff, and omit `mode` if you do not require a specific mode.

## Next step

Use [Company profile](/api-reference/extract-company-profile) for the organization-focused guidance, or [Email finder](/api-reference/email-finder) to enrich a person profile.

---

## Company profile

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/extract-company-profile.md

Description: Extract a structured company profile from a company profile URL.

Extract a structured organization profile from a recognized LinkedIn `/company/` or `/school/` URL.

<Note>
The limit is 3,000 requests per minute per workspace. The submitted URL selects the response schema and successful-call credit cost: `/company/` and `/school/` successes cost 0.5 credits, while `/in/` successes cost 1 credit by default. Workspace-specific pricing can differ, and unsuccessful requests are not charged.
</Note>

The optional modes are `p1`, `p2`, and `p3`. Omit `mode` for the default extraction workflow, whose successful shape can vary; use `p2` or `p3` when you need the normalized schema. The submitted URL, not the route name, selects company versus person output.

Extraction failures return an error rather than a `200 OK` no-result envelope. Retry transient extraction or settlement failures with bounded backoff, and omit `mode` if you do not require a specific mode.

## Next step

Use [People profile](/api-reference/extract-people-profile) for the person-focused guidance, or [Find companies](/api-reference/find-companies) to discover organizations first.

---

## Reverse email

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/reverse-email.md

Description: Find a person profile from an email address.

Submit an email address and receive the matching person profile when one can be resolved.

<Note>
The limit is 25 requests per second per workspace. A returned profile costs 2 credits. A miss returns the JSON string `"not found"`, not an object with a status field, and is not charged.
</Note>

After a `429 Too Many Requests` response, retry in a later second with bounded exponential backoff. A `503` transport or settlement failure is not charged; retry the same email with bounded backoff after the dependency recovers.

## Next step

Use [Reverse phone](/api-reference/reverse-phone) when a phone number is the identifier you have for a person.

---

## Reverse phone

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/reverse-phone.md

Description: Find a person profile from a phone number.

Submit a phone number and receive the matching person profile when one can be resolved.

<Note>
The limit is 2,000 requests per minute per workspace. A returned profile costs 10 credits; `not_found` and errors are not charged.
</Note>

A `not_found` result can represent a true miss or lookup paths that were exhausted or failed. When a match is expected, make one bounded-backoff retry. If it persists, verify that you sent the intended normalized number before retrying again.

Wait for the credit service to recover before retrying a settlement failure with the same number.

## Next step

Use [People profile](/api-reference/extract-people-profile) when you already have a professional profile URL and want the structured profile directly.

## Credit count

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/credit-count.md

Description: Check the remaining credit balance for your Airscale workspace.

Read the remaining credit balance for the workspace associated with your API key before starting paid enrichment work.

<Note>
Send no request body. Checking the balance is free and does not debit Airscale credits.
</Note>

An invalid or missing key returns `401 Unauthorized`. Confirm the current key in the Airscale dashboard and update your server-side secret; rotate it only if it was exposed.

## Next step

Use your authenticated client to [find people](/api-reference/find-people), or review [Authentication](/api-reference/authentication) before sending requests.

## How to use the Airscale MCP (+Claude demo)

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp.md

Description: Prospect through conversation with Airscale search, enrichment, and export tools.

Prospect without leaving your AI chat. Airscale connects Claude, ChatGPT, and other compatible assistants to search, enrichment, research, and export tools, so you can build a list through natural-language conversation.

<Frame>
  <iframe
    className="w-full aspect-video rounded-xl"
    src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/t4coJ0P8YVM"
    title="How to prospect with Airscale MCP in Claude"
    allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
    referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    allowFullScreen

</Frame>

## What is the Airscale MCP?

The Airscale MCP gives your assistant 22 typed tools that can:

- Check your workspace credit balance.
- Search for people and companies.
- Discover valid Find Companies filters before searching.
- Enrich contact details and person or company profiles.
- Run Airsearch for structured web research.
- Create downloadable CSV or JSONL exports.

See the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools) for every tool and its inputs.

## How credits work

Find People costs 0.1 credit per returned person. Find Companies costs 0.1 credit per returned company. Airsearch costs 2 credits per call.

Credit checks, people counts, and Find Companies filter discovery are free planning tools. Other enrichment follows linked API pricing in the related references for [contact data](/api-reference/email-finder), [people profiles](/api-reference/extract-people-profile), and [company profiles](/api-reference/extract-company-profile).

Before a paid export starts, review the final filters, row limit, and maximum spend, then explicitly confirm that paid action. No paid search, enrichment, or export should run before your approval.

## Run a search in natural language

Describe the cohort and keep the first result small. The example prompts below are illustrative and non-executing; they instruct your assistant to pause before every paid action.

> Find up to five cybersecurity companies in France with 51–200 employees. Before you run it, show me the proposed tool, filters, row limit, and maximum cost, then wait for my approval.

Your assistant can use a free filter-discovery tool first when a value needs validation. Approve only the bounded search you reviewed.

### Review your results

Review the company name, domain, website, country, and filter precision before expanding the search. At 0.1 credit per returned company, a five-company sample costs at most 0.5 credits.

### Enrich contacts through conversation

Begin with a bounded role-discovery request for only the companies you approved:

> Discovery step: For the approved companies, discover at most one CEO, one CFO, and one Head of Growth per approved company. Show me the proposed tool, per-step maximum cost, and cumulative workflow maximum, then wait for my approval.

Review the discovered people and approve the decision-makers you want to continue with. Then request only their professional work emails:

> Professional work email enrichment step: For only the approved decision-makers, find professional work emails. Show me the proposed tool, contact count, per-step maximum cost, and new cumulative workflow maximum, then wait for my approval.

Review the requested fields and linked pricing before approving each stage. Keep each follow-up bounded, and do not add unapproved companies or contacts to the request.

## Export your final list

People and company exports perform a fresh paid search from the final filters. They do not export the selected chat rows, may return different rows, and add a new charge in addition to earlier paid steps in the workflow.

Before starting, require the assistant to repeat the exact filters, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum, then wait for your approval.

Exports are asynchronous: start one export, check its status, then retrieve the file after completion. Save the returned `export_id` and reuse the same `export_id` for status and file requests.

Follow the `poll_after_seconds` interval returned by each status response. Do not start a duplicate export while the existing job is queued or running.

## Get started

- [Connect Airscale MCP to ChatGPT](/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-chatgpt)
- [Connect Airscale MCP to Claude](/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-claude)
- [Read the Airscale MCP server reference](/mcp/airscale-mcp-server)

## Connect Airscale MCP to ChatGPT

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-chatgpt.md

Description: Connect ChatGPT to Airscale through browser OAuth and validate the connection without spending credits.

Connect ChatGPT to your Airscale workspace with browser OAuth, then verify the connection with a free tool call before you approve any paid work.

## MCP server URL

Use the official remote MCP endpoint exactly as shown:

```text
https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp
```

## What ChatGPT can do with Airscale MCP

Airscale MCP gives ChatGPT 22 typed tools that can:

- Check the authorized workspace's credit balance.
- Search for people and companies.
- Count matches and discover accepted filter values before a paid search.
- Enrich work contact details and extract people or company profiles.
- Run Airsearch web research.
- Create downloadable people or company exports.

Managed large contact enrichment is work-email-only in its current phase. Review exact inputs and credit behavior in the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools).

## Before you start

You need an Airscale account with access to the intended workspace, API access enabled, and an active workspace credential. ChatGPT uses browser OAuth for this connection: the browser asks you to sign in to Airscale, choose a workspace, and authorize ChatGPT.

ChatGPT web supports the full MCP flow documented here for Business and Enterprise/Edu workspaces:

- **Business:** An admin or owner must enable developer mode and create the custom app. Developer access cannot currently be delegated to an ordinary Business member.
- **Enterprise/Edu:** Admins and owners can use RBAC to grant developer mode to an authorized developer. Admins or owners still control publication and workspace access.

Pro accounts can use custom apps with read/fetch permissions, but this full MCP setup requires Business or Enterprise/Edu. Check OpenAI's current [developer mode and MCP apps guide](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461) if availability or labels differ.

After OAuth, Airscale's MCP server resolves the authorized workspace's current credential server-side on each tool call; ChatGPT neither receives nor stores that API key. Do not paste an Airscale API key into ChatGPT, prompts, or tool inputs.

## Step-by-step setup

<Steps>
  <Step title="Enable the app creation controls">
    In Business, sign in as an admin or owner and open **Workspace settings → Apps → Create**. In Enterprise/Edu, use an admin/owner account or an account with developer-mode access through RBAC, then open the available **Apps → Create** control.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Enter the Airscale endpoint">
    Name the app **Airscale MCP** and enter `https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp` as its MCP endpoint. Complete any other metadata required by the current form.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Choose OAuth and scan the tools">
    Select **OAuth**, then click **Scan Tools** and complete the Airscale OAuth flow in the browser: sign in and select the intended workspace. Return to ChatGPT and wait for the scan to finish before continuing. The ChatGPT connection does not need a copied secret or static authorization value.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Create the draft">
    Click **Create** only after the scan succeeds. The draft app appears in the workspace's draft-app list and in the creator's enabled apps.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select Airscale for a message">
    Open a new chat and select the draft app from the tools menu, or mention it in your prompt. The selection applies to that message, not the entire conversation, so select or mention Airscale again when a follow-up needs another tool call.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Verify the connection for free">
    Ask ChatGPT to use `airscale_check_credits` and no other tool. A returned balance confirms tool discovery and authentication to an Airscale workspace without debiting credits. It does not identify which workspace; verify the workspace shown during OAuth before paid actions.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Recommended first prompts

The identities and domains below are synthetic.

> Use `airscale_check_credits` to show my current Airscale credit balance. Do not call another tool.

This is the free connection test. A returned balance confirms tool discovery and authentication to an Airscale workspace without debiting credits. It does not identify which workspace; verify the workspace shown during OAuth before paid actions.

> Count people named Jordan Example who work at `northstar.example`. Do not run a paid search.

> Plan an Airscale search for up to five companies matching `sample-company.test`. Show the proposed Airscale tool, arguments, and maximum cost, then wait for my approval.

For a complete staged sequence, follow the [safe MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp).

## Export behavior in ChatGPT

A people or company export performs a fresh paid search from the final filters; it does not package the selected chat rows and may return different rows. Before approval, review the exact filters, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum.

An export has one asynchronous lifecycle: start the export once, check its status, then retrieve the file when it is ready. Reuse the same `export_id` and honor the returned `poll_after_seconds`. Do not start a duplicate export while the original job is queued or running.

## Credits and confirmation

The credit check, people count, company filter-value discovery, export status, and export-file retrieval are free. Search and enrichment tools can consume credits; Airsearch costs 2 credits per call. Managed contact enrichment is work-email-only in its current phase.

Paid export starts fail closed until `confirm_credit_spend` is explicitly `true`. Review ChatGPT's proposed tool, arguments, row limit, and maximum cost before confirming. An export can support up to 10,000 rows, but use the smallest limit that serves the task.

## Refreshing tools

If Airscale tools are stale or missing, refresh or reconnect the app and start a new conversation so ChatGPT scans the current tool list. Re-select the draft app for the message that should use it.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Custom MCP controls are not visible">
    Confirm that the ChatGPT account and workspace expose custom remote MCP apps. A Business admin or owner may need to enable the feature; Enterprise/Edu access may depend on RBAC.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Scan Tools does not complete">
    Confirm the exact server URL, finish the Airscale browser authorization, and return to ChatGPT. Remove and reconnect the draft while signed in to the intended Airscale workspace if the scan stays pending.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Authentication succeeds but a tool fails">
    Confirm that the selected Airscale workspace has API access, an active workspace credential, and enough credits for the proposed paid tool. Run `airscale_check_credits` before retrying.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="An export remains queued">
    Poll `airscale_get_export_status` with the same identifier and the returned `poll_after_seconds`. Do not create another paid job.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Security note

Authorize only the Airscale workspace you intend to use. Keep secrets out of chats and tool inputs, review every proposed paid action, and remove the app's access when it is no longer needed.

## Need help?

- Review the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools) for exact schemas and credit behavior.
- Use the [safe MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp) before running a search or export.
- Read the [Airscale MCP server overview](/mcp/airscale-mcp-server) for authentication and security guidance.

## Connect Airscale MCP to Claude

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-claude.md

Description: Connect Claude clients to Airscale with hosted OAuth or a protected Claude Code authorization header.

Connect Claude to your Airscale workspace through hosted remote OAuth where supported, or configure Claude Code with a protected environment-backed header.

## MCP server URL

Use the official remote MCP endpoint exactly as shown:

```text
https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp
```

## What Claude can do with Airscale MCP

Airscale MCP gives Claude 22 typed tools that can:

- Check the authorized workspace's credit balance.
- Search for people and companies.
- Count matches and discover accepted filter values before a paid search.
- Enrich work contact details and extract people or company profiles.
- Run Airsearch web research.
- Create downloadable people or company exports.

Managed large contact enrichment is work-email-only in its current phase. Review exact inputs and credit behavior in the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools).

## Before you start

You need an Airscale account with access to the intended workspace, API access enabled, and an active workspace credential.

Claude web and desktop clients can use remote OAuth in the browser where supported by the Claude account and client. Each hosted user signs in to Airscale and authorizes a workspace.

Claude Code can instead use a protected authorization header sourced from an environment variable. Hosted OAuth and Claude Code header authentication are separate connection methods. Never put the credential in a prompt or MCP tool argument.

## Claude web setup

Use the hosted connector flow that matches your Claude account. If availability or labels differ, check Anthropic's current [remote custom connector guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp).

### Individual Claude accounts

Individual Free, Pro, or Max accounts can add a custom connector directly. A Free account is limited to one custom connector.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open connector settings">
    Sign in to Claude web or desktop and open **Customize → Connectors**. Use the current connectors or integrations settings if the label differs.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add Airscale">
    Choose the control to add a custom connector, name it **Airscale MCP**, and enter `https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp` as the remote server URL.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Authorize your Airscale workspace">
    Continue to the browser sign-in, authenticate with Airscale, select the intended workspace, approve access, and return to Claude.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Enable the tools">
    Select Airscale MCP for a new conversation and confirm that Claude can see its tools.
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Claude Team and Enterprise

For Claude Team or Enterprise, an Owner or Primary Owner must add Airscale through **Custom → Web** before members can connect.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Owner adds the organization connector">
    Open **Organization settings → Connectors**, choose **Add**, hover over **Custom**, select **Web**, and enter `https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp`. Add the connector to the organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Each member authorizes Airscale">
    Each member opens **Customize → Connectors**, finds Airscale MCP, clicks **Connect**, and authenticates with their own Airscale account in the browser.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Each member enables the tools">
    Select Airscale MCP and the tools needed for the conversation. Organization approval makes the connector available; it does not share an Owner's Airscale authorization with members.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Claude Code setup

Load `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` through an OS or team secret manager or a protected runtime environment before starting Claude Code. Do not type a literal API key into a shell command or shell history.

Create a project-scoped `.mcp.json` at the project root:

```json Project .mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "airscale": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${AIRSCALE_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `${AIRSCALE_API_KEY}` expression is resolved from the Claude Code process environment. Never replace it with a literal secret in `.mcp.json`; each developer supplies the environment value independently.

From the project root, verify that Claude Code loaded the server:

```bash
claude mcp list
```

Inside Claude Code, run `/mcp` to inspect connection status and the available tools. See the official [Claude Code MCP scope documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) before choosing a different scope; local and user configurations live in `~/.claude.json`, not in the project file.

## Recommended first prompts

The identities and domains below are synthetic.

> Use `airscale_check_credits` to show my current Airscale credit balance. Do not call another tool.

This is the free connection test. A returned balance confirms tool discovery and authentication to an Airscale workspace without debiting credits, but it does not identify which workspace. Hosted users must verify the OAuth-selected workspace, and Claude Code users must verify which workspace owns the configured credential before paid actions.

> Use Airscale MCP to count people named Taylor Example at `northstar.example`. Do not run a paid search.

> Plan an Airscale search for up to five companies matching `sample-company.test`. Show the proposed Airscale tool, arguments, and maximum cost, then wait for my approval.

For a complete staged sequence, follow the [safe MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp).

## Export behavior

A people or company export performs a fresh paid search from the final filters; it does not package the selected chat rows and may return different rows. Before approval, review the exact filters, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum.

An export has one asynchronous lifecycle: start the export once, check its status, then retrieve the file when it is ready. Reuse the same `export_id` and honor the returned `poll_after_seconds`. Do not start a duplicate export while the original job is queued or running.

## Credits and confirmation

The credit check, people count, company filter-value discovery, export status, and export-file retrieval are free. Search and enrichment tools can consume credits; Airsearch costs 2 credits per call. Managed contact enrichment is work-email-only in its current phase.

Paid export starts fail closed until `confirm_credit_spend` is explicitly `true`. Review Claude's proposed tool, arguments, row limit, and maximum cost before confirming. An export can support up to 10,000 rows, but use the smallest limit that serves the task.

## Refreshing tools

If Airscale tools are stale or missing, refresh or reconnect the hosted connector and start a new conversation. In Claude Code, verify the environment and server with `claude mcp list`, then use `/mcp` to inspect the refreshed connection.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Hosted connector controls are unavailable">
    Confirm that the Claude client and account support remote MCP connectors. In Team or Enterprise, ask an Owner or Primary Owner to add Airscale before each member connects their own account.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="OAuth opens but the connection stays pending">
    Complete the Airscale browser sign-in, wait for the authorization confirmation, and return to Claude. Reconnect while signed in to the intended workspace if the state does not update.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Claude Code reports an authentication error">
    Confirm that the environment variable is available to the Claude Code process and that the project configuration uses the `Bearer` scheme. Do not print the value while debugging.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="An export remains queued">
    Poll `airscale_get_export_status` with the same identifier and the returned `poll_after_seconds`. Do not create another paid job.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Security note

Hosted Claude users should authorize only the Airscale workspace they intend to use. Claude Code users should keep the environment value out of version control, prompts, and tool inputs. For either method, review every proposed paid action and remove access when it is no longer needed.

## Need help?

- Review the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools) for exact schemas and credit behavior.
- Use the [safe MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp) before running a search or export.
- Read the [Airscale MCP server overview](/mcp/airscale-mcp-server) for authentication and security guidance.

## Airscale MCP Server

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/mcp/airscale-mcp-server.md

Description: Connect Airscale to your AI assistant and prospect without leaving the chat.

Airscale MCP gives compatible AI assistants a concise, typed interface for prospecting through conversation while keeping authentication and paid actions explicit.

## MCP server URL

```text
https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp
```

This remote Streamable HTTP server works with hosted assistants and trusted developer clients. For hosted clients, OAuth is preferred and uses browser sign-in. The Airscale MCP server resolves the authorized workspace credential server-side; the client neither receives nor stores the API key.

Trusted header-capable developer clients must load `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` from a protected runtime environment or secret manager. Never place a literal API key in a prompt or tool argument, source or browser code, or a shell command or shell history.

## Getting started

1. First, choose the setup guide for your assistant.
2. Then connect it to the MCP server URL above.
3. Complete browser OAuth or authenticate from a protected developer runtime.
4. Select and verify the intended workspace.
5. Run `airscale_check_credits` as the free connection check before any paid tool.

The credit check confirms authentication to an Airscale workspace without debiting credits, but it does not identify which workspace. Verify the workspace selected during OAuth—or the workspace that owns a developer credential—before paid actions.

## Setup walkthroughs

- [ChatGPT setup guide](/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-chatgpt)
- [Claude setup guide](/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-claude)
- [Airscale MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp)

These guides contain the client-specific connection steps; this page keeps the shared server contract in one place.

## What you can do

- **People and companies search:** discover prospects with bounded, structured searches.
- **Filter discovery:** inspect available filters and counts before requesting rows.
- **Contact and profile enrichment:** add professional contact details or public person and company profiles.
- **Airsearch:** answer natural-language research questions with structured results.
- **Downloadable exports:** create bounded people, company, or managed contact files and retrieve them when complete.

The [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools) is the schema reference for all 22 typed tools. Managed contact enrichment is a work-email-only flow; it does not add mobile numbers, personal emails, or profile enrichment.

## Export lifecycle

### People and company exports

People and company exports are fresh paid searches, not packages of selected chat rows. A people export uses the final `query`; a company export uses the final `filters`. Results may differ from the sample, and each export creates an additional charge.

Before confirming, review the final scope, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum. At up to 0.1 credits per exported row, the requested limit defines the maximum for this fresh search. Set `confirm_credit_spend` only after that review.

### Managed contact enrichment export

A managed contact enrichment export starts from a frozen `batch_id`. Review the approved contact count, `work_email` as the only enrichment, fields and format, and the maximum calculated as the approved contact count multiplied by up to 2 credits per contact. Review that additional maximum together with the cumulative workflow maximum, then set `confirm_credit_spend` only after approval.

### One export lifecycle

Both branches use one asynchronous lifecycle:

1. Use the branch's **start** tool once. Keep the returned `export_id`, and do not start a duplicate export while the job is queued or running.
2. Check **status** with the same `export_id` and respect `poll_after_seconds`.
3. Retrieve the **file** with the same `export_id` only after completion.

## How credits work

- Free operations include the credit check, planning, people count or company filter discovery, export status polling, and completed file retrieval.
- Find People and Find Companies each cost 0.1 credit per returned row.
- Airsearch costs 2 credits per call.
- The managed work-email-only contact enrichment phase costs up to 2 credits per contact.
- Paid export starts fail closed until `confirm_credit_spend` is explicitly set after review.

For exact per-tool behavior, use the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools).

## Recommended workflow

1. Run `airscale_check_credits` for a free connection check.
2. Verify the intended workspace before choosing a paid path.

### People and company search/export

1. Use a free count or filter discovery tool to plan the request.
2. Run a bounded sample and inspect the returned shape.
3. Review the workspace, results, and credit implications before continuing.
4. For optional enrichment, request separate approval with its own maximum and updated cumulative spend.
5. Before exporting, perform a renewed export review of the final `query` or `filters`, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum.
6. Set `confirm_credit_spend` only after approval, then start once.

### Managed contact enrichment/export

1. Finish the free batch-building steps, then keep the frozen `batch_id`.
2. Review the approved contact count, `work_email`, fields and format.
3. Calculate the maximum from the approved contact count multiplied by up to 2 credits per contact.
4. Review the additional maximum and cumulative workflow maximum, then set `confirm_credit_spend` only after approval.

### Finish either export

Start once, then poll the same export job through status and file retrieval using the same `export_id` and `poll_after_seconds`. Do not start it again.

## Security notes

- OAuth keeps workspace credential resolution server-side; the hosted client does not receive or store the Airscale API key.
- Header-capable developer clients should read `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` only from a protected runtime environment or secret manager.
- Never put a literal key in prompts, tool arguments, source control, browser code, shell commands, or shell history.
- Verify the intended workspace before paid actions because a credit balance alone does not identify it.
- Review every paid tool name, scope, and maximum cost before approval.
- If a developer API key is exposed or suspected compromised, rotate it immediately, update the protected secret, and reconnect every trusted client that used it.
- Treat tokenized export URLs and exported files as sensitive. Never place them in prompts or logs, and follow your organization's access, retention, and deletion rules.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="The client cannot authenticate">
    For OAuth, restart browser sign-in and verify the intended workspace. For a header-capable developer client, confirm that its protected runtime can read the configured secret.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="The Airscale tools do not appear">
    Confirm that the server URL is exactly `https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp`, then disconnect and reconnect so the client refreshes all 22 tools.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="A request reports insufficient credits">
    Run `airscale_check_credits`, reduce the paid scope, and review the maximum again. Do not repeatedly submit the same paid request.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="An export is still running">
    Continue polling the same `export_id` at `poll_after_seconds`. Do not create a duplicate while its outcome is unknown.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
